description:
The Phase 1 launch corpus is 6 bundles, all at scale factor 0.01. This is
enough to prove the explorer renders, but too small to look credible to a
visitor evaluating real-world performance. The strategy doc commits to
"depth per benchmark" - ≥3 comparable platforms per cohort - and SF 0.1
is the next rung that exercises the platforms beyond toy timings while
staying within reasonable runtime + storage budgets for CI / local runs.

This item generates SF 0.1 cohorts for TPC-H and SSB on the same three
platforms each cohort already covers at SF 0.01 (TPC-H: DuckDB, DataFusion,
Polars; SSB: DuckDB, DataFusion, SQLite), uses the production submit→PR
flow to land them on `published-results`, and confirms the explorer
renders the new cohort selectors.

anti_patterns.dont: bypass `benchbox submit` and copy bundles directly into `results-data/bundles/`
anti_patterns.why: the production flow (submit + manifest + CI) needs to be exercised on every cohort, not just community ones.
the generator from `automate-corpus-inventory-generation` is now authoritative.

anti_patterns.dont: skip platforms where a few queries fail and ship partial-coverage bundles
anti_patterns.why: the cohort's value is in apples-to-apples comparison; partial coverage misleads.

preserves.behavior: Cohort isolation - SF 0.01 and SF 0.1 must remain separate cohorts in the explorer.
Maintainer-run trust label on all generated bundles (no fake community labels).

verifications.description: Inventory contains 12 bundles total (6 SF 0.01 + 6 SF 0.1)
Each new bundle validates against schema-v2

work_units.notes:
For each platform run a clean tuned run, using full TPC-H query set:
  benchbox run --platform duckdb     --benchmark tpch --scale 0.1 --tuning tuned
  benchbox run --platform datafusion --benchmark tpch --scale 0.1 --tuning tuned
  benchbox run --platform polars-df  --benchmark tpch --scale 0.1 --tuning tuned
Capture environment metadata (uname, CPU, RAM) in the bundle. If a
query fails on a given platform, document the failure in
`_project/notes/` and leave the bundle out (don't ship a partial
cohort that misleads the compare view).
work_units.summary: Generate TPC-H SF 0.1 results on DuckDB, DataFusion, Polars

work_units.notes:
Same pattern as w1. SQLite at SF 0.1 may be slow; allow extended
timeouts but do not silently shorten the query set:
  benchbox run --platform duckdb     --benchmark ssb --scale 0.1 --tuning tuned
  benchbox run --platform datafusion --benchmark ssb --scale 0.1 --tuning tuned
  benchbox run --platform sqlite     --benchmark ssb --scale 0.1 --tuning tuned
work_units.summary: Generate SSB SF 0.1 results on DuckDB, DataFusion, SQLite

work_units.notes:
For each bundle:
  benchbox submit --last --output ./submission-<platform>-<benchmark>-sf0.1/
Verify the manifest hash and the labelled trust label is `maintainer-run`
(these are not community submissions).
work_units.summary: Package each bundle with `benchbox submit` and stage the PR

work_units.notes:
Single PR is preferable to 6 PRs because:
  - the cohort is meaningful only when complete,
  - the explorer rebuild only fires once per merge,
  - reviewers see all SF 0.1 results together.
Confirm validate-submission CI passes; address any failures.
Confirm corpus-inventory.json regenerates cleanly (depends on
automate-corpus-inventory-generation). Merge after review.
work_units.summary: Open a single submission PR against published-results with all 6 bundles

work_units.notes:
After explorer redeploy:
  - TPC-H scale-factor selector lists 0.01 and 0.1
  - SSB scale-factor selector lists 0.01 and 0.1
  - Compare view at /results/compare?ids=<3 SF 0.1 ids> renders
  - Cohort validation does NOT block within-SF comparisons
  - Cohort validation DOES block mixed-SF comparisons
Capture one screenshot per benchmark of the SF 0.1 compare view.
work_units.summary: Verify the explorer surfaces the new SF 0.1 cohort
